description: Experience the grandeur of a traditional Middle Eastern feast with our Lamb Ouzi, a magnificent whole slow roasted lamb dish. This celebratory meal features tender, fall-off-the-bone lamb infused with aromatic spices, served atop a fragrant bed of spiced rice and garnished with toasted nuts. Perfect for special occasions, Lamb Ouzi promises an unforgettable culinary journey to the heart of the Levant.

ingredients.item: Ouzi spice blend (7-spice, cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger)

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb leg or shoulder dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make several deep slits all over the lamb. In a small bowl, mix olive oil, Ouzi spice blend, salt, and black pepper to create a paste. Rub this paste generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the slits.

instructions.title: Marinate and Roast
instructions.text: Place the seasoned lamb in a large roasting pan. Cover tightly with foil and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight. Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Roast the lamb, covered, for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until it is very tender and easily pulls from the bone. Remove the foil for the last 30 minutes to allow the exterior to brown slightly.

instructions.title: Rest the Lamb
instructions.text: Once roasted, remove the lamb from the oven and transfer it to a large serving platter. Tent it loosely with foil and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more tender and flavorful meat. Reserve any pan juices for drizzling.

instructions.title: Prepare the Spiced Rice
instructions.text: While the lamb rests, melt ghee or butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sauté for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the rinsed basmati rice, peas, diced carrots, and 1 tablespoon of the Ouzi spice blend. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, coating the rice.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice
instructions.text: Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Fluff the rice gently with a fork.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Arrange the cooked spiced rice on a large serving platter. Carefully place the whole slow roasted lamb on top of the rice. Drizzle with any reserved pan juices. Garnish generously with toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately as a magnificent centerpiece for your Middle Eastern feast.

tips: For the most tender lamb, ensure slow roasting at a low temperature for several hours until the meat easily pulls away from the bone. Over-roasting can dry out the meat.
Adjust the spice blend in the rice to your preference, adding a touch more cinnamon or cardamom for a warmer flavor profile, or a pinch of chili for a subtle kick.
Leftover Ouzi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in the oven or microwave, adding a splash of broth if the rice seems dry.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East, where food is not just sustenance but a celebration of family, tradition, and exquisite flavors. Among the most revered dishes gracing tables at festive gatherings and special occasions is Lamb Ouzi, a magnificent centerpiece that epitomizes slow-roasted perfection. This article will guide you through the art of preparing whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi, a dish that promises to transform your dinner party into an unforgettable feast.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?
Lamb Ouzi is a quintessential Middle Eastern dish, often considered the crown jewel of celebratory meals. While variations exist across the Levant, Gulf, and other parts of the Arab world, the essence remains the same: tender, succulent lamb, often a whole leg or shoulder, slow-roasted to fall-off-the-bone perfection. It's traditionally served atop or alongside a rich, aromatic rice pilaf, studded with toasted nuts, sometimes minced meat, and delicate spices. The name "Ouzi" itself refers to this grand preparation, a dish synonymous with hospitality and generosity. The slow roasting process is critical, breaking down the tough fibers of the lamb over hours, infusing it with deep flavors from a potent marinade, and rendering it incredibly juicy and tender. Preparing Lamb Ouzi is an act of love, resulting in a dish that is as visually stunning as it is delicious.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi
Crafting the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients and a pantry stocked with essential Middle Eastern spices.

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole lamb leg (about 5-7 lbs/2.5-3.5 kg), bone-in preferred for flavor, or a large lamb shoulder
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   Juice of 2 lemons
*   8-10 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tablespoons ground cumin
*   2 tablespoons ground coriander
*   1 tablespoon sweet paprika
*   1 tablespoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1 teaspoon ground allspice
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   Salt to taste (approximately 2-3 tablespoons, adjust based on size)
*   Bay leaves (optional, for roasting pan)
*   Fresh rosemary or thyme sprigs (optional)

For the Ouzi Rice (Pilaf):
*   2 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   1 tablespoon olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 lb (450g) ground lamb or beef (optional, for a richer pilaf)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
*   1/4 cup pine nuts
*   1/4 cup slivered almonds
*   1/2 cup frozen peas (optional)
*   1/2 cup diced carrots (optional)
*   3 cups hot chicken or vegetable broth
*   Salt and black pepper to taste

For Garnish:
*   Fresh parsley, chopped
*   Extra toasted pine nuts and almonds

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi
Preparing this magnificent dish is a labor of love, but the steps are straightforward and the reward is immense.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the lamb leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the surface of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep. This helps the marinade penetrate and fat render. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, black pepper, and salt. Rub this marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover it, and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, preferably 24-48 hours, allowing the flavors to deeply infuse.
2.  **Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. You can add a few bay leaves and rosemary sprigs to the bottom of the pan for extra aroma. Cover the pan tightly with foil. Roast for 4-5 hours, depending on the size of your leg, or until the internal temperature reaches about 145°F (63°C) for medium-rare, or 160°F (71°C) for well-done (it will continue to cook).
3.  **Crisp the Lamb:** Remove the foil, increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C), and continue roasting for another 45-60 minutes, or until the exterior is beautifully browned and crispy. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. The lamb should be incredibly tender, almost falling off the bone.
4.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once roasted, remove the lamb from the oven, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest on a cutting board for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. This crucial step allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and moist result.
5.  **Prepare the Ouzi Rice:** While the lamb rests, prepare the rice. In a large pot or deep skillet, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Add pine nuts and almonds and toast until golden brown, then remove and set aside. Add the chopped onion to the same pot and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. If using ground meat, add it now and cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon. Drain any excess fat.
6.  **Season and Cook Rice:** Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot, along with cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper. Stir well to coat the rice with spices. Pour in the hot broth. If using, stir in the frozen peas and diced carrots. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during this time.
7.  **Fluff and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the rice from heat and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Then, gently fluff with a fork. Stir in most of the toasted nuts.
8.  **Assemble the Lamb Ouzi:** On a large serving platter, spread the aromatic Ouzi rice. Carefully place the whole slow-roasted lamb leg on top of or alongside the rice. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and the remaining toasted nuts.

## Pro Tips for the Best Lamb Ouzi
Achieving perfection with your Lamb Ouzi is within reach with a few expert tips:

*   **Quality Lamb:** Start with good quality, fresh lamb. Bone-in cuts tend to offer more flavor and moisture retention during the long cooking process.
*   **Marination is Key:** Do not rush the marination. The longer the lamb sits in the spice mixture (up to 48 hours), the deeper and more complex its flavor will be.
*   **Low and Slow Roasting:** This is non-negotiable for tender lamb. A low oven temperature allows the connective tissues to break down slowly, resulting in meat that literally falls off the bone.
*   **Rest the Meat:** Always rest the lamb after roasting. This allows the muscle fibers to relax and reabsorb the juices, ensuring a more succulent and flavorful cut.
*   **Toast Nuts Separately:** For the rice, toast the pine nuts and almonds separately before adding them to the rice or as a garnish. This enhances their flavor and prevents them from burning.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks quickly. Follow the instructions precisely and avoid lifting the lid to ensure fluffy, separate grains.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi
Lamb Ouzi is a showstopper on its own, but traditional accompaniments elevate the experience and balance the rich flavors.

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple, cooling yogurt sauce (such as labneh or a plain yogurt with mint and garlic) provides a refreshing contrast to the richness of the lamb.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Crisp, vibrant salads like Fattoush (bread salad) or Tabbouleh (parsley and bulgur salad) add freshness and acidity.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (torshi) offer a tangy counterpoint that cuts through the richness.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Perfect for scooping up any remaining rice and juices.
*   **Beverages:** Serve with traditional Arabic coffee, mint tea, or a refreshing glass of ayran (a savory yogurt drink).

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi
While the classic Lamb Ouzi is a masterpiece, you can explore variations to suit your taste or available ingredients.

*   **Lamb Cut:** If a whole lamb leg is too large, you can use a bone-in lamb shoulder, which also benefits from slow roasting. For smaller gatherings, individual lamb shanks can be slow-cooked with similar spices.
*   **Stuffing the Lamb:** Some traditional Ouzi recipes involve stuffing the lamb cavity with the spiced rice mixture before roasting. This requires a larger cavity and careful sealing.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to adjust the spice levels. Add a pinch of cayenne pepper for heat, or more cinnamon for a warmer flavor profile.
*   **Rice Additions:** Experiment with other dried fruits like apricots or currants in the rice, or different nuts like pistachios for color and texture. For a healthier touch, increase the amount of peas and carrots.
*   **Cooking Method:** While oven roasting is common, some traditional methods involve pit roasting for an incredibly smoky flavor. For smaller cuts, a slow cooker can also be used, though it won't achieve the crispy exterior.

Creating whole slow-roasted Lamb Ouzi is a culinary adventure that yields a truly spectacular result. It's a dish that embodies warmth, generosity, and the rich tapestry of Middle Eastern flavors, making it the perfect centerpiece for your next special occasion. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the tender, spice-infused lamb that will leave a lasting impression on your guests.
